region.name: Payments Team 1on1 Notes
region.summary: Manager 1on1 and skip-level notes on Payments engineers Marcus, Sarah, Devon, and Sam, covering the ACH cut-over with Pillar, single-point-of-failure risk, ownership gaps, retention concerns, and post-Series B comp commitments.

brief.text:
This region collects the manager's 1:1 and skip-level notes on the Payments team: Marcus Bell (lead), Sarah Kim, Devon, and Sam. The central thread is the ACH pipeline rebuild and cut-over with the banking partner Pillar. Marcus and the manager decided on a minimum of 12 days in shadow mode, with the cut-over date set with Pillar in June. Sarah joined Payments and had a skip-level four weeks in. She found shadow-mode diff triage a good onboarding exercise but reported that the onboarding guide is stale on the Sidekiq ACH path. Her most important observation was that Marcus is a single point of knowledge for Pillar ops. The manager had been treating that as a compliment rather than a risk. Marcus later asked to hand the Pillar sync to Sarah. Sarah also flagged legacy money-moving Rails/Sidekiq jobs that have no owner and no idempotency story.

The largest open risk is the round-up sweep job. It runs on Rails/Sidekiq without idempotency keys through Q3 (severity 29). Ownership of the job is unclear between Payments and Growth, and the team made a conscious decision to defer moving it onto the new pipeline. A related open todo is closing the KYC migration from Persona to Alloy (owner Hana, severity 27). Marcus's September week off is gated on that migration closing. Other operational items include:

- ADR-024 PR reviews are bottlenecked on the manager. The fix is blocked review windows on Tuesday and Thursday.
- Rails monolith grumbling persists. The plan is to carve out money movement and raise it at all-hands.
- Hiring pipeline frustration led to a referral bonus, which is still an open commitment, and a contract sourcer.
- A VP Eng search is engaged via Hollis Partners, intended to take operational load off Marcus.

People and retention concerns run throughout. Marcus burnout is tracked as an open risk, logged three times with severity 4, including burnout before the VP Eng starts. He is described as stretched but energized. He has asked for formal ownership of Payments & Platform and is owed a significant comp adjustment after a clean ACH launch and the Series B close. The manager is watching his frustration with the comp wait. Devon is seen as the top flight risk. He is informally sketching a nightly ledger reconciliation job against bank and broker records, and the manager intends to let him pitch it himself; his post-Series B comp adjustment must land right. Sam is quiet, precise, and strong but will not escalate unprompted. The manager plans biweekly check-ins with him until the SOC 2 gaps close. Marcus's next learning goal is interview design. Typical questions this region answers include who owns Pillar ops or the round-up sweep, the shadow-mode and cut-over plan, outstanding comp commitments, who is a flight risk, and the status of the KYC and SOC 2 work.

items.title: Decision: Give Marcus a significant comp adjustment after clean ACH launch
items.summary: Manager notes the company owes Marcus a significant adjustment once the new ACH pipeline ships cleanly.

items.title: Decision: Rotate diff review from day one next time
items.summary: Marcus wants shadow-period diff review to be a rotation rather than his personal sign-off.

items.title: Open Question: When will legacy money-moving jobs move to the new pipeline
items.summary: Sarah asked when the Rails money-moving jobs will move to the new pipeline. The answer is eventually, with no date.

items.title: Open Question: Who owns the round-up sweep job end to end?
items.summary: Payments and Growth overlap: Growth changes multiplier logic while Payments gets paged. A joint session with Kavi is to draw the line.
